kept.q: An element P (atomic number 11) reacts with an element Q (atomic number 17) to form a compound. Which of the following best describes the bonding and structure of the resulting compound?
options: Covalent bonding with a simple molecular structure
Ionic bonding with a giant crystal lattice structure
Metallic bonding with a sea of delocalised electrons
Dative bonding with a discrete molecular structure
kept.explanation: Sodium (atomic number 11) is a metal that easily loses one electron, while chlorine (atomic number 17) is a non-metal that readily gains one electron. The transfer of electrons forms oppositely charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces in a giant ionic lattice.
kept.pidgin: Sodium na metal wey dey easily loss one electron, while chlorine na non-metal wey dey gain one electron. E form giant ionic lattice because of strong electrostatic force between the ions.

kept.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why ionic compounds generally have higher melting points than simple covalent molecular compounds?
options: Ionic compounds have weaker van der Waals forces between molecules
Ionic compounds contain strong electrostatic forces acting in all directions throughout the lattice
Ionic compounds exist as discrete molecules with low molecular mass
Ionic compounds share electrons equally between bonded atoms
kept.explanation: In ionic compounds, each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions and is held by strong electrostatic attraction in every direction throughout the giant lattice. This requires a lot of energy to overcome, unlike the weak intermolecular forces in simple covalent molecules.
kept.pidgin: For ionic compounds, strong electrostatic attraction dey everywhere inside the giant lattice. Na why e dey take plenty energy to break am, unlike simple covalent molecules.

kept.q:
Using the bond energy values below, calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction: H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2HCl(g).
Bond energies (kJ/mol): H-H = 436, Cl-Cl = 243, H-Cl = 431
options: -183 kJ/mol
+183 kJ/mol
-679 kJ/mol
+679 kJ/mol
kept.explanation: Enthalpy change equals bonds broken minus bonds formed: (436 + 243) - (2 x 431) = 679 - 862 = -183 kJ/mol. The negative sign shows the reaction is exothermic since more energy is released forming new bonds than used breaking old ones.
kept.pidgin: To calculate am, you go minus the bonds formed from the bonds broken, wey give us (436 + 243) minus (2 times 431). The minus sign show say energy release, meaning the reaction na exothermic.

kept.q: Consider a molecule of boron trifluoride, BF3, where boron is the central atom. Boron has 3 valence electrons and each fluorine contributes one electron to each B-F bond. According to Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory, what is the expected shape of BF3?
options: Tetrahedral
Trigonal planar
Trigonal pyramidal
Bent (V-shaped)
kept.explanation: Boron in BF3 has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs around the central atom. With three regions of electron density and no lone pair repulsion, the molecule adopts a trigonal planar shape with bond angles of 120°.
kept.pidgin: Boron for BF3 get three bonding pairs and no lone pair at all. Because of this, the molecule go carry trigonal planar shape with 120° bond angle.

kept.q: Element W has the electronic configuration 2,8,2 while element Z has the configuration 2,8,7. If W and Z combine to form a stable compound, what is the simplest formula of the compound and the type of bond formed?
options: WZ2, ionic bond
W2Z, ionic bond
WZ2, covalent bond
W2Z7, covalent bond
kept.explanation: Element W (configuration 2,8,2) loses 2 electrons to form W2+ and element Z (configuration 2,8,7) gains 1 electron to form Z-. To balance charges, one W2+ ion combines with two Z- ions, giving the formula WZ2, and the electron transfer between a metal-like and non-metal-like species makes it ionic.
kept.pidgin: W go loss 2 electrons to form W2+, while Z go gain 1 electron to form Z-. To balance everything, you need one W and two Z, wey make the formula WZ2 with ionic bond.

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why metals are good conductors of electricity in both solid and molten states?
options: Metal ions are held together by strong covalent bonds that allow electron flow
Metals contain mobile delocalised electrons that can move freely through the structure
Metals have giant ionic lattices with freely moving ions in all states
Metals form simple molecular structures with weak intermolecular forces
kept.explanation: In metallic bonding, the valence electrons are delocalised and not fixed to any particular atom, forming a sea of electrons that can move freely. This free movement of electrons allows metals to conduct electricity whether solid or molten.
kept.pidgin: Metals get electrons wey dey free to move anyhow inside the structure like sea of electrons. Na this free movement dey make them conduct electricity well.

kept.q: A student is comparing the boiling points of hydrogen chloride (HCl) and hydrogen fluoride (HF). Despite HF having a lower molar mass than HCl, HF has a significantly higher boiling point. What is the most likely reason for this observation?
options: HF molecules have stronger covalent bonds within the molecule than HCl
HF experiences hydrogen bonding between molecules while HCl does not
HF has more delocalised electrons than HCl
HF is an ionic compound while HCl is covalent
kept.explanation: Fluorine is highly electronegative and small, allowing HF molecules to form strong hydrogen bonds between molecules, unlike HCl which only has weaker dipole-dipole and van der Waals forces. These extra hydrogen bonds in HF require more energy to break, giving it a higher boiling point despite its lower molar mass.
kept.pidgin: HF get strong hydrogen bonding because fluorine small and electronegative well well, but HCl no get am. Na why HF boiling point high pass HCl even though e get small molar mass.

q.q: In the formation of a water molecule, oxygen shares two pairs of electrons with two hydrogen atoms. Which term describes the type of covalent bond present in each O-H bond, considering only one shared pair is involved per bond?
options: Coordinate bond
Single covalent bond
Double covalent bond
Triple covalent bond
q.explanation: Each O-H bond in water consists of one shared pair of electrons, with each atom contributing one electron to the pair. This is the definition of a single covalent bond.
